auth.keyHelp: In Entra ID > App registrations > New registration, then Authentication > Allow public client flows = Yes; no client secret is needed. Add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, Files.Read.

signIn.clientHelp: 1) Sign in at https://entra.microsoft.com as at least Application Developer. 2) Entra ID > App registrations > New registration; name it; Supported account types: 'Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts' if you also want a personal Outlook.com account, otherwise 'Single tenant only'. Register, then copy Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID from Overview. 3) Manage > Authentication > Advanced settings > Allow public client flows = Yes > Save. No secret, no redirect URI needed for device code. 4) Manage > API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated: User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, Files.Read. 5) In the app, paste the client ID and tenant; it shows a short code and the page to open (verification_uri); open it on any device and sign in.

read.label: List files in the top of OneDrive
List files in a OneDrive folder

notes: DEVICE CODE: Microsoft supports it with a public client (Authentication > Allow public client flows = Yes) and no client secret; request POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/devicecode with client_id and scope, then poll POST .../oauth2/v2.0/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. The user has 15 minutes by default. verification_uri_complete is not supported, so the person types the user_code. Poll no faster than the interval; errors to expect: authorization_pending, authorization_declined, bad_verification_code, expired_token. A refresh_token is returned only if offline_access is requested; default refresh token lifetime is 90 days (24 hours for SPA redirects). TENANT CONFLICT (unresolved): the device-code protocol page says tenant 'can be /common, /consumers, or /organizations' (or a tenant ID) and even describes the personal-account re-sign-in under /common or /consumers; but the MSAL desktop device-code page's sample comment says 'AADSTS90133: Device Code flow is not supported under /common or /consumers endpoint'. Safest, consistent with both pages: use 'organizations' or the Directory (tenant) ID for work/school accounts. For a personal Microsoft account the right tenant value is NOT confirmed (the protocol page implies consumers works; the MSAL page says it does not); test it before promising it. CONDITIONAL ACCESS: Microsoft recommends organizations block device code flow where it is not needed (Conditional Access > Authentication flows > Device code flow > Block). A managed work tenant may therefore refuse this sign-in; nothing the app can do, an admin must allow it. CONSENT: the permissions reference shows Calendars.Read and Files.Read as delegated with AdminConsentRequired = No and available to personal Microsoft accounts; Mail.Read and User.Read were checked in the same reference earlier in this run and also need no admin consent for delegated use, but the Mail.Read table row was not re-read for this manifest. The Graph pages list Mail.ReadBasic and Calendars.ReadBasic as the LEAST privileged permissions for messages/calendarView; what fields they omit (likely bodies) was not read, so Mail.Read and Calendars.Read are used for full content. Higher write scopes are NOT in signIn.scopes: send_mail needs Mail.Send, create_event needs Calendars.ReadWrite; add them only if writes are wanted. App registration: Entra requires at least Application Developer; registration page does not give a deep link to App registrations, hence keyUrl is the admin center home. Account types on the registration page: single tenant, multiple Entra tenants, any Entra tenant + personal Microsoft accounts, personal only. Graph base https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0 appears in the example URLs on the Graph pages. $top is a standard OData option; the messages and calendarView pages say they support the OData query parameters, but $top was not named individually. MCP: Microsoft's official Work IQ MCP server is remote at https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp, authenticated with Microsoft Entra ID (clients discover config via /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource), tools like fetch /me/messages. Its overview page is dated 2026-10-05; a Work IQ licence or Copilot requirement was NOT confirmed on the pages read, and availability can vary by tenant, region and admin policy per the Agent 365 page, so a plain personal account may not get it. Older workload MCP servers (Mail, Calendar, OneDrive, SharePoint) are called a legacy experience for testing and backward compatibility. No call was made.
